schema.projects: primary key (id,user_id); updated_at timestamptz client-writable before M14.5; metadata jsonb after 202608240002
schema.conversations: primary key (id,user_id); updated_at timestamptz client-writable before M14.5
schema.messages: primary key (id,user_id); created_at only; FK to conversation owner with cascade
schema.knowledge_items: primary key (id,user_id); updated_at timestamptz client-writable before M14.5
schema.user_preferences: primary key (user_id,preference_key); value jsonb; updated_at client-writable before M14.5
schema.rls: all listed tables enable RLS with one owner policy: using/with check user_id = auth.uid()
schema.triggers_before: no updated_at or revision trigger in the repository migrations

timestamp_findings.stale_write_protection: works when the timestamp actually changes and differs
timestamp_findings.same_millisecond_collision: two clients can use the same millisecond; the second condition can match, allowing a lost update
timestamp_findings.client_supplied_timestamp: the update payload includes the client updated_at; it can fail to advance
timestamp_findings.zero_row_delete: M14.4 delete did not inspect affected rows, so a conditional delete that matched nothing could be reported as applied
timestamp_findings.rls_vs_missing_row: M14.4 mapped all read errors to retry_required; a 401/403 was not classified as authentication_required

correction.mechanism: continuity_revision bigint + lelu_continuity_touch() BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on projects, conversations, knowledge_items, user_preferences
properties: client cannot choose the new revision
correction.fallback: adapter reads continuity_revision when present; a project without the migration falls back to updated_at with a monotonic client timestamp
correction.token_format: rev:<n> for strict revisions; ts:<timestamp> for legacy fallback; plain M14.4 timestamps remain accepted

defects_fixed: lost insert acknowledgement retried into a false conflict; now content-equal retry is applied
lost update acknowledgement with an old base retried into a conflict; now content-equal retry is applied
first sync of a hydrated cloud record enqueued an upload with expected=null; now adopted or rebased
a pre-engine local edit newer than the cloud copy is rebased onto the observed cloud revision
document changes caused by another record no longer conflict when the target record is still at its base hash
conditional delete now verifies that a row was actually deleted
conversation message retries use ignoreDuplicates so a lost ack cannot overwrite a newer message
residual_limits: the revision migration must be applied to the real project before strict atomic acceptance
messages have no independent revision; the conversation row remains the conditional boundary
the OG server functions still write conversations directly and are outside the continuity engine
document-backed authorities share a row-level revision; separate records rebase only when the target record is unchanged
real cloud execution is BLOCKED by missing isolated credentials
